groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 21 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

SK Group and NVIDIA are launching a strategic partnership worth over 500 billion dollars to build AI infrastructure for global compute demand. As part of this initiative, SK Telecom will construct a two-gigawatt AI factory using the NVIDIA DSX platform and Vera Rubin accelerated computing powered by SK hynix HBM4 memory. The first factory is expected to come online in 2027 to support sovereign, agentic, and enterprise AI services across the Asia-Pacific region. While these industrial expansions scale up, individual researchers are navigating the academic side of the field. On Reddit, a contributor to the Neurips Position Paper Track shared their experience receiving reviews for a first-time conference paper submission. The researcher noted that their meta review included actionable requirements for revision and is now seeking community advice on how to write rebuttals to convince reviewers to change their scores.

Fire is pushing closer to Bordeaux in southwest France. Authorities ordered the evacuation of new communes on Saturday as a precaution against the advancing flames. This crisis follows a series of massive forest fires across France and Spain since mid-week that have forced more than 200,000 people from their homes. In Gironde, roughly 3,500 evacuees from the Arcachon basin and nearby towns are now staying at the Bordeaux exhibition center. The facility has been converted into a reception hub where two large hangars provide food, clothing, and cots for those displaced. Meanwhile, Bison Futé is urging motorists to avoid entering or crossing through the Gironde department entirely. This measure aims to keep roads clear for emergency services as they battle the fires during a high-risk weather alert.

Karim Khan has been removed from his position as Chief Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court. The court's member states voted in New York to dismiss the British lawyer following allegations of sexual abuse made by a former employee. While Khan firmly denies the claims, the assembly cited serious misconduct and a grave violation of official duties. This departure comes after Khan had sought an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in the Gaza war. Meanwhile, unprecedented wildfires are forcing mass evacuations across Southern Europe. In France, roughly 141,000 people have been moved to safety as flames threaten the city of Bordeaux. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez stated that the country has never seen fires of this magnitude. Spain is facing similar devastation, with authorities in Madrid ordering 25,000 residents to evacuate because the fires there have become uncontrollable.

Millions of people in Germany remain completely offline as the world around them grows increasingly digital. According to data from the Federal Statistical Office, roughly three percent of residents between 16 and 74 years old have never used the internet. This gap is most visible among older populations; while no official comparative data exists for those over 75, other studies suggest they are even less likely to be active online. The divide persists across other age groups too, with three percent of people aged 45 to 64 and one percent of those between 25 and 44 reporting no online experience. Media scientist Moritz Büchi notes that statistics can be misleading, as someone who only checks email occasionally is still counted as an onliner. This means the two million people who have never used the web are joined by many others who lack meaningful digital participation.

In Ukraine, officials in the Kyiv region have declared a day of mourning following a Russian attack on July 24th. The observance includes limiting entertainment events and flying flags at half-mast across the province. Meanwhile, in West Africa, Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana are attempting to increase their bargaining power in the global cocoa trade through the CIGCI initiative. Presidents Alassane Ouattara and John Mahama met in Abidjan on June 16th to coordinate farm-gate prices and capture more value for producers. In a separate matter of political record, fact-checkers have corrected a claim made by Alternative National Congress Secretary General Desmond Nimely during a live interview on Focal TV. While Nimely alleged that the Collaborating Political Parties won five seats in the 2020 senatorial election, statistics from the National Elections Commission show the CPP actually won six seats.

In New Delhi, youth-led protests at Jantar Mantar are entering their 36th day as the Cockroach Janta Party calls for a nationwide candle march this Sunday. While a second round of talks between the movement and the Indian government is scheduled for today, protesters say they will remain in the streets until Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns over a paper leak scandal. Police have tightened security as crowds are expected to swell over the weekend with office-goers joining the demonstrations. Meanwhile, in San Francisco, Samsung Electronics and Broadcom signed a memorandum of understanding at the AI Summit to expand their collaboration on memory and foundry technologies. The partnership is estimated at more than 200 billion dollars through 2030, focusing on High Bandwidth Memory for AI accelerators and Samsung’s 2-nanometer process for wireless broadband communications and advanced packaging.

Wildfires are sweeping through southwest France, fueled by tinder-box dry conditions and extremely high winds. The blazes have already hit two major areas, forcing tourists to evacuate and threatening the city of Bordeaux. In one instance, fire swept through 2,000 hectares near a popular tourist hotspot. These escalating conditions have created what some describe as a recipe for disaster for the region. As a result, more than 40,000 people have been forced to evacuate their homes and hotels to escape the flames. The situation remains critical as emergency services struggle to contain the fires in the vulnerable southwest landscape.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be clear with temperatures between 24 and 28 degrees and rain chances up to 20 percent.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day, and a dinner invitation at six in the evening.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
